"""One image, detected once, filtered many times: the engine behind the browser page (web/).

  s = Session('slide.tif')          load the channels and the blue (DAPI) mask
  s.detect('tl')                    the slow part: a finder proposes candidates and measures each one
  s.refilter({'values': {...}, 'off': [...]})
                                    the fast part: the checks, the nucleus rule and one-pixel-per-NoR
                                    run again on the stored measurements (milliseconds)

The blue (DAPI) mask is only ever a filter here ('in nucleus'), never applied before finding.

The filters are not listed here. They are read from nor3.CHECKS, so a check added there, with its
parameters read through `p[...]` or `p.get(...)`, shows up on the page as a control by itself; its
letter and text come from nor3.REASONS and nor3.REASON_TEXT.

Refiltering reproduces a finder's own result exactly when the finder judges each candidate on its
own (tl, fill, walk, blobs). rf chooses between alternative greens using the checks, so after a
filter change it is an approximation until detect() runs again with the new values; at the finder's
own values it returns the finder's own result.
"""
import ast, inspect, json, math
import numpy as np
import nor3, naive_nor as nn_, nor_lab
from nor3 import CHECKS, ORDER, REASONS, REASON_TEXT, judge, resolve_overlaps

# the finders the page offers, first = default
FINDERS = {'tl': 'traffic light', 'rf': 'red-first', 'fill': 'fill', 'walk': 'walk', 'blobs': 'blobs'}
EXACT_REFILTER = {'tl', 'tl_post', 'fill', 'walk', 'blobs'}
# finders that take the blue mask themselves and apply it only after finding; every other finder
# sees no mask, so nuclei are left to the 'in nucleus' filter
OWN_BLUE = {'rf', 'tl_post'}
# failures that come after the checks and have their own parameter (their defaults when a finder has none)
NUCLEUS, SHARED = 'in nucleus', 'shares a segment'
POST = {NUCLEUS: ('nucleus_frac', 0.8), SHARED: ('max_shared', 0.3)}
REASON_TEXT.setdefault(NUCLEUS, 'red mostly on a nucleus (blue mask, applied after finding)')
REASONS.setdefault(NUCLEUS, ('N', (90, 140, 255)))


def check_params():
    """{check: {param: default}}, read from the source of nor3.CHECKS. A default is the one given
    to p.get(); None means the finder's parameter set must supply it."""
    tree = ast.parse(inspect.getsource(nor3))
    node = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and getattr(n.targets[0], 'id', '') == 'CHECKS')
    out = {}
    for k, v in zip(node.value.keys, node.value.values):
        ps = {}
        for n in ast.walk(v):
            if isinstance(n, ast.Subscript) and getattr(n.value, 'id', '') == 'p' and isinstance(n.slice, ast.Constant):
                ps.setdefault(n.slice.value, None)
            elif (isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute) and n.func.attr == 'get'
                  and getattr(n.func.value, 'id', '') == 'p' and isinstance(n.args[0], ast.Constant)):
                ps[n.args[0].value] = n.args[1].value if len(n.args) > 1 else None
        out[k.value] = ps
    return out


def _num(v):
    v = float(v)
    return round(v, 6) if math.isfinite(v) else None


class Session:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.caspr, self.nav, self.um, dapi = nn_.load(path)
        self.bm = nn_.blue_mask(dapi)
        self.dapi = dapi
        self.cands, self.P, self.finder = [], {}, None

    def images(self):
        """red, green, blue (8-bit display stretch) and the blue mask, H*W bytes each, in that order."""
        return b''.join([nn_.to8(self.nav).tobytes(), nn_.to8(self.caspr).tobytes(), nn_.to8(self.dapi).tobytes(),
                         self.bm.astype(np.uint8).tobytes()])

    def detect(self, finder='tl', overrides=None):
        """Run a finder with its parameters (plus overrides). Returns (meta JSON, segment bytes): each
        candidate's segments are an h*w block at meta offset `off`, 1 = red, 2 and 3 = the greens."""
        fn, P = nor_lab.finders()[finder]
        self.P = dict(P, **(overrides or {})); self.finder = finder
        bm = self.bm if finder in OWN_BLUE else np.zeros_like(self.bm)
        self.cands, info = fn(self.caspr, self.nav, bm, self.P)
        H, W = self.caspr.shape
        """The controls: one per check in judging order, then the nucleus rule and one-pixel-per-NoR."""
        cp = check_params(); out = []
        for k in ORDER + [c for c in CHECKS if c not in ORDER] + list(POST):
            ps = cp[k] if k in CHECKS else {POST[k][0]: POST[k][1]}
            vals = {n: self.P.get(n, d) for n, d in ps.items()}
            out.append(dict(key=k, letter=REASONS.get(k, ('?',))[0], text=REASON_TEXT.get(k, k),
                            params={n: v for n, v in vals.items() if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool)}))
        return out

    def detection_params(self):
        """Every other scalar parameter of the finder: changing one means detecting again."""
        used = {n for f in self.filters() for n in f['params']}
        return {k: v for k, v in self.P.items() if k not in used and isinstance(v, (int, float, str, bool, tuple, list))}

    def refilter(self, spec):
        """spec: {'values': {param: value}, 'off': [filter keys]}. Returns each candidate's result:
        None for a pass, else the failure reason."""
        values = spec.get('values', {}); p = dict(self.P, **values); off = set(spec.get('off', []))
        ours = {n: v for f in self.filters() for n, v in f['params'].items()}
        if self.finder not in EXACT_REFILTER and all(ours.get(n, v) == v for n, v in values.items()) and not off:
            # the finder's own result, so the page opens on exactly what the lab scores
            for c in self.cands:
                c['fail'] = c['fail_found']
            return [c['fail'] for c in self.cands]
        order = [k for k in ORDER if k not in off] + [k for k in CHECKS if k not in ORDER and k not in off]
        for c in self.cands:
            c['fail'] = c['fail0']
            judge(c, p, order)
            if c['fail'] is None and NUCLEUS not in off and c['red_on_blue'] >= p.get('nucleus_frac', POST[NUCLEUS][1]):
                c['fail'] = NUCLEUS
        if SHARED not in off:
            resolve_overlaps(self.cands, self.caspr.shape, p.get('max_shared', POST[SHARED][1]))
        return [c['fail'] for c in self.cands]

content.content:
## R8 — The NoR Finder page: detect once, filter live, in the browser

Set by the owner on 2026-09-28. The page is [`web/`](../web/), served from GitHub Pages with no
backend. Its engine is [`detection/interactive.py`](../detection/interactive.py), tested by
[`tests/test_interactive.py`](../tests/test_interactive.py).

- **One image, one slow step.** Opening an image loads it and runs a finder once. Everything else
  (filters, forced markings, the list, the summary) redraws from the stored candidates without
  finding again.
- **Filters are live dials.** Every check in `nor3.CHECKS`, the nucleus rule (N) and
  one-pixel-per-NoR (J) is a control that can be switched off. Each of its parameters is a dial, and
  every marking on the image follows it at once. A check added to `CHECKS` becomes a control with
  no page change.
- **Detection settings are dials too.** They re-run the finder, and the page says that this takes
  time.
- **All finders are offered.** Traffic light is the default.
- **The blue mask is only a filter.** No finder on the page blanks nuclei before finding.
- **The list and the summary.** Every passing NoR is shown cropped, with its measurements, and
  the measurements are summarised below the list. A starred candidate stays in the list whatever
  the filters say. A candidate the user removes stays in the list, greyed out, and is left out of
  the totals.
- **Fixed numbers.** Each candidate keeps one number, top to bottom, for as long as a detection
  lasts. Filters never renumber candidates.
- **Remembered marks.** Stars and removals are saved in the browser per file name and finder, tied
  to each candidate's position.
- **Visible waiting.** While Python loads and while a finder runs, the page shows a spinner and
  the elapsed time.
- **Remembered settings.** Filter settings persist in the browser across images, visits and
  days, and one button restores the defaults.
- **Only our code is fetched fresh.** Third-party code (Pyodide, its packages, vendored wheels)
  is cached in the browser for 30 days.
- **The page runs the lab's code.** The Python it runs is the repo's `detection/` and `src/` as
  they are, so the finder stays malleable. At our settings, the page passes what the lab passes
  with the blue mask applied after finding.
29:- **Browser page** (`web/`, requirement R8): open an image, detect once, then tune every filter
31:  Pages through the github-pages pack. Preview it locally with `python3 web/build.py` and then
32:  `python3 -m http.server` from the repo root, opening `/web/`.
66:| browser/ | runs the finders in a browser runtime (Pyodide): measured parity, recommendation |

{"number":228,"title":"Page fixes: slides with red-displayed DAPI, fixed numbers, greyed removals, saved marks, spinner","body":"<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- Some slides failed to load, on the page and in the lab, with "DAPI detected on a green/red channel".
- On the page, candidate numbers changed with every filter change.
- "remove" dropped a NoR from the list, and a reload forgot the marks.
- Nothing moved while Python loaded or a finder ran.
- Unticking "measuring lines" did nothing.

After:
- Every fetched slide loads: 32 of 32, where 4 "Up Middle" slides failed before.
- Each candidate keeps one number, top to bottom, for the whole detection. A rejected one shows its number plus its letter, e.g. "12D".
- A removed NoR stays in the list, greyed out, with a "restore" button, and is left out of the totals.
- Stars and removals are saved in the browser per file name and finder.
- A spinner and an elapsed-time counter show while the page loads and while a finder runs.
- Unticking "measuring lines" hides them.

Why the slides failed: in the R,G,B files DAPI is displayed red, and the loader took the red-displayed channel to be Nav1.6.

How:
- `naive_nor.load` picks channels by role, as `data/README.md` prescribes. Caspr is the green-displayed channel, DAPI is whichever of the other two has larger blobs, and Nav1.6 is the rest. Slides that loaded before get the same channels. This also fixes the one file where the README says the blob test failed.
- The page numbers candidates once per detection.
- Marks are keyed by the candidate's rounded position under `nor-marks-v1:<file>|<finder>`.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` gains the new points.

Checks:
- `tests/test_load_channels.py` fails on main (4 slides) and passes here.
- `tests/test_interactive.py` passes, with the same 247 passes on the reference slide.
- In Chromium: 0 numbers moved across a filter change; a remove and a star survived a reload; the spinner showed during loading and finding; lines, labels and rejected candidates each hide when unticked.

_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- Some slides failed to load, on the page and in the lab, with "DAPI detected on a green/red channel".
- On the page, candidate numbers changed with every filter change.
- "remove" dropped a NoR from the list, and a reload forgot the marks.
- Nothing moved while Python loaded or a finder ran.
- Unticking "measuring lines" did nothing.
- The page ran the finder as soon as an image loaded. Everything was stacked in one column: controls on the left, the image, then the list and the summary further down.

After:
- Every fetched slide loads: 32 of 32, where 4 "Up Middle" slides failed before.
- Each candidate keeps one number, top to bottom, for the whole detection. A rejected one shows its number plus its letter, e.g. "12D".
- A removed NoR stays in the list, greyed out, with a "restore" button, and is left out of the totals.
- Stars and removals are saved in the browser per file name and finder.
- A spinner and an elapsed-time counter show while the page loads and while a finder runs.
- Unticking "measuring lines" hides them.
- The page is laid out in these parts:
  - **Header:** a logo slot, the title and a remembered dark/light switch.
  - **Left bar:**
    - the image box: load, file name, and one checkbox per colour layer, with blue off at first;
    - the candidates finder: the algorithm, its main settings, a collapsed Advanced box with every setting, and a Find Candidates button;
    - the filters.
  - **Main area:** a toolbar (zoom, overlay options, and a big button that switches between the image and the individual items) over the two views.
  - **Right bar:** the summary.
  - **Status bar:** the image name, the candidate and finalist counts, and the time each step took.
- Loading an image no longer runs the finder. Find Candidates shines until it is pressed, and again whenever the finder or its settings change.

Why the slides failed: in the R,G,B files DAPI is displayed red, and the loader took the red-displayed channel to be Nav1.6.

How:
- `naive_nor.load` picks channels by role, as `data/README.md` prescribes. Caspr is the green-displayed channel, DAPI is whichever of the other two has larger blobs, and Nav1.6 is the rest. Slides that loaded before get the same channels. This also fixes the one file where the README says the blob test failed.
- The page numbers candidates once per detection.
- Marks are keyed by the candidate's rounded position under `nor-marks-v1:<file>|<finder>`.
- Each finder function declares its main settings in a `MAIN` tuple. `interactive.describe(finder)` gives the page a finder's filters and settings before it runs.
- `web/logo.svg` is a plain "TAU" placeholder until the real logo file replaces it.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` gains the new points.

Checks:
- `tests/test_load_channels.py` fails on main (4 slides) and passes here.
- `tests/test_interactive.py` passes, with the same 247 passes on the reference slide. Its new main-settings test fails without the `MAIN` declarations.
- In Chromium, on the old fixes:
  - 0 numbers moved across a filter change;
  - a remove and a star survived a reload;
  - the spinner showed during loading and finding;
  - lines, labels and rejected candidates each hide when unticked.
- In Chromium, on the new layout:
  - the button shines after a load and after a finder change, and not after a run;
  - main and Advanced settings stay in sync;
  - clicking a finalist rejects it and clicking again restores it (247 → 246 → 247);
  - the theme survives a reload.

---
name: repo-is-home
description: Ariel's rule - all code, instructions, skills and current state live in missingbulb/NoRFinder; project folders hold only temporary artifacts
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Ariel (2026-09-28): "Don't ever keep things only in project folders except processing artifacts. The project is just a tool to help the repo grow, never the objective." Processing code, instructions, skills, labels, the ledger and the current state all go into the repo in a PR, as part of the same change.

**Why:** a session starting from the repo couldn't see three days of NoR work that lived only in /mnt/project-files.
**How to apply:** work in the repo's `detection/` (STATE.md, lab/ledger.md, finders, tools). There is no NoR-specific skill (Ariel: fold learnings into the generic image-algorithm-development skill); NoR criteria are docs/requirements.md R7. The rule "Where the work lives" is in the local pack RULES.md (PR #221). /mnt/project-files/nor-detection/ is only for renders and caches. Before calling work done, check that nothing needed exists only in the project.

---
name: provenance-once-per-pr
description: Ariel wants one Claudinite provenance entry per element per PR, not one per commit
metadata:
  type: feedback
  modified: 2026-09-27T17:34:44.024Z
---

Ariel (2026-09-27): a pack element's provenance file gets one entry per PR. The ideal would be one per released version, but that is harder to do. When a PR revises the same element several times, squash its entries into a single one before merge, with `Landed: #<pr>`. An element that is new in the PR gets a single `born` entry.

**Why:** a new entry for every commit in one PR clutters the append-only log.
**How to apply:** while a PR is open, the provenance file can still be edited, so rewrite that PR's entries as one. After merge, only append. See [[image-algorithm-skill]].

---
name: nor-qa-preferences
description: Ariel's review image format is an API - render with render_std.py (v8 style), never change without approval
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Ariel (2026-09-25): the yellow QA outline must hug the detected element (a thick wand, green-red-green) with a thin line, not an ellipse or circle. The blue (DAPI) mask areas are approved as ignore-zones for NoR detection.

**Why:** they judge false positives and negatives by eye, and loose ellipses hide which pixels were detected.
**How to apply:** naive_nor.py element_mask() traces Caspr|Nav foreground at 0.7x the detection thresholds along each node's axis, then draws a 1-px ring on a 3x upscale. Keep this style for new overlays. See [[blue-mask-implemented]].

Update 2026-09-25 (later): Ariel asked for the outlines to be blue at 40% transparency, with the red-segment outline even more transparent. NoRs are numbered top to bottom, and a list (length, red length, ratio) is added beside the image. nor3.py main() implements this.

Update 2026-09-25 22:17: Ariel wants every filtering stage visible in the final image. All candidates are drawn, with pass = pink outline and fail = blue outline. Each is numbered top to bottom, and each failure gets a coloured letter for its reason: A one green, B greens joined, C not in a line, D red impure, E green impure, F greens unequal, G not stick-like. A legend and a list of all candidates sit in a side panel. Red specks with no adjacent green are not drawn. Output: all_candidates/.

Update 2026-09-25 23:35: accepted NoRs also show their measuring lines in white. The length line is 1 px along the green-to-green axis, and its stretch over the red is 2 px. The width line is 1 px, crosses the red centre, and is as long as the mean width. See measure() c['lines'] in nor3.py.

Update 2026-09-27: Ariel treats the review format as an API. The v9 thread switched to a yellow-only outline because the older index line said "yellow", and Ariel objected. From now on:
- Produce review images only with nor-detection/render_std.py SPEC OUTDIR. It writes overlay_all_candidates.png, overlay_zoom_with_legend.png (crop x900-2100, y1200-2400 at 3x, plus a 500-px legend) and nor_candidates.csv, exactly as for v8.
- Don't change colours, crosses, letters or the crop. Propose any improvement and wait for approval.

cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/db11916e-d354-5299-be26-942076491f31/scratchpad && cat > tracelogo.py <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, potrace
from PIL import Image
S = 4
im = Image.open('logo_src.png').convert('L').crop((0, 30, 447, 185))
big = np.array(im.resize((im.width * S, im.height * S), Image.BICUBIC)) < 128
parts = [(15, 152, '#e53935'), (154, 297, '#2e9e44'), (298, 440, '#2f6fe0')]
paths = []
ys, xs = np.nonzero(big)
x0, y0, x1, y1 = xs.min(), ys.min(), xs.max() + 1, ys.max() + 1
for a, b, col in parts:
    m = np.zeros_like(big); m[:, a * S:b * S] = big[:, a * S:b * S]
    plist = potrace.Bitmap(m).trace(turdsize=8, alphamax=1.0, opticurve=True, opttolerance=0.2)
    d = []
    f = lambda p: f"{(p.x - x0) / S:.2f} {(p.y - y0) / S:.2f}"
    for c in plist:
        d.append("M" + f(c.start_point))
        for s in c.segments:
            d.append(("L" + f(s.c) + "L" + f(s.end_point)) if s.is_corner else ("C" + f(s.c1) + " " + f(s.c2) + " " + f(s.end_point)))
        d.append("Z")
    paths.append(f'<path fill="{col}" fill-rule="evenodd" d="{"".join(d)}"/>')
W, H = (x1 - x0) / S, (y1 - y0) / S
open('logo.svg', 'w').write(f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W:.0f} {H:.0f}">' + "".join(paths) + "</svg>\n")
print(W, H, len(open('logo.svg').read()))
EOF

{"number":228,"title":"Page: new layout, Find Candidates on demand, plus fixes for red-displayed DAPI, numbering and marks","body":"<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- Some slides failed to load, on the page and in the lab, with "DAPI detected on a green/red channel".
- On the page, candidate numbers changed with every filter change.
- "remove" dropped a NoR from the list, and a reload forgot the marks.
- Nothing moved while Python loaded or a finder ran.
- Unticking "measuring lines" did nothing.
- The page ran the finder as soon as an image loaded. Everything was stacked in one column: controls on the left, the image, then the list and the summary further down.

After:
- Every fetched slide loads: 32 of 32, where 4 "Up Middle" slides failed before.
- Each candidate keeps one number, top to bottom, for the whole detection. A rejected one shows its number plus its letter, e.g. "12D".
- A removed NoR stays in the list, greyed out, with a "restore" button, and is left out of the totals.
- Stars and removals are saved in the browser per file name and finder.
- A spinner and an elapsed-time counter show while the page loads and while a finder runs.
- Unticking "measuring lines" hides them.
- The page is laid out in these parts:
  - **Header:** a logo slot, the title and a remembered dark/light switch.
  - **Left bar:**
    - the image box: load, file name, and one checkbox per colour layer, with blue off at first;
    - the candidates finder: the algorithm, its main settings, a collapsed Advanced box with every setting, and a Find Candidates button;
    - the filters.
  - **Main area:** a toolbar (zoom, overlay options, and a big button that switches between the image and the individual items) over the two views.
  - **Right bar:** the summary.
  - **Status bar:** the image name, the candidate and finalist counts, and the time each step took.
- Loading an image no longer runs the finder. Find Candidates shines until it is pressed, and again whenever the finder or its settings change.

Why the slides failed: in the R,G,B files DAPI is displayed red, and the loader took the red-displayed channel to be Nav1.6.

How:
- `naive_nor.load` picks channels by role, as `data/README.md` prescribes. Caspr is the green-displayed channel, DAPI is whichever of the other two has larger blobs, and Nav1.6 is the rest. Slides that loaded before get the same channels. This also fixes the one file where the README says the blob test failed.
- The page numbers candidates once per detection.
- Marks are keyed by the candidate's rounded position under `nor-marks-v1:<file>|<finder>`.
- Each finder function declares its main settings in a `MAIN` tuple. `interactive.describe(finder)` gives the page a finder's filters and settings before it runs.
- `web/logo.svg` is a plain "TAU" placeholder until the real logo file replaces it.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` gains the new points.

Checks:
- `tests/test_load_channels.py` fails on main (4 slides) and passes here.
- `tests/test_interactive.py` passes, with the same 247 passes on the reference slide. Its new main-settings test fails without the `MAIN` declarations.
- In Chromium, on the old fixes:
  - 0 numbers moved across a filter change;
  - a remove and a star survived a reload;
  - the spinner showed during loading and finding;
  - lines, labels and rejected candidates each hide when unticked.
- In Chromium, on the new layout:
  - the button shines after a load and after a finder change, and not after a run;
  - main and Advanced settings stay in sync;
  - clicking a finalist rejects it and clicking again restores it (247 → 246 → 247);
  - the theme survives a reload.

# public-website pack

Being a public website, whatever serves it: the version the site carries and the stamp its pages show, and the ways a page that fetches its own data goes quietly stale. **Opt-in**: a project declares it when it publishes a site, beside the pack for whatever hosts the site. Nothing here builds, serves or releases anything, and nothing here names a host: a hosting pack's release reaches [`public/version.mjs`](public/version.mjs) to advance the version as part of cutting a release, and goes out without a bump when the file is absent.

## The version

`<major>.<ymmdd>.<build>`, computed and never typed: the major is a generation statement raised by hand, the middle part is the UTC release date counted in years from 2025, and the build is a monotonic counter. `package.json` is the one record; a page opts into showing the version by carrying `title="version …"` on the element that should show it, and the bump stamps every tracked page that does. The scheme, the stamp and the set of files a bump rewrites live in [`public/version.mjs`](public/version.mjs); [`bump-version.mjs`](bump-version.mjs) is its working-tree caller, with `--stamp-only` as the drift repair.

## Checks

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public-website/version-stamp-matches-package` | medium | correctness | check: blocking |

What it holds: every tracked page carrying a stamp names `package.json`'s version.

## Rules (`RULES.md`)

| Rule | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| The version stamp is generated, never typed | medium | correctness | prose: <50 words + check (`public-website/version-stamp-matches-package`) |
| Freshness is a published manifest's job | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Nothing attests to its own freshness | high | correctness | prose: <50 words |
| Split caches join across generations | critical | correctness | prose: <100 words |
| Follow missing data to the pixel | high | correctness | prose: <100 words |

The last four are the client-side half: the four ways a page that fetches its own data goes stale quietly.

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- In Ariel's browser the logo showed huge, the status bar was tall, and the whole page scrolled.
- Windows narrower than 1100 px stacked the columns.
- The site version was not shown anywhere.

After:
- The frame is fixed. The 52 px header, the three columns and a 1 cm footer fill the window exactly, and only the left bar, the main box and the right bar scroll. Narrower windows get narrower side bars instead of stacked columns.
- The logo is 36 px high inside the header.
- The footer ends with the site version, e.g. "v1.0.0". It shows 1.0.0 until the first release after this merges.

Stale files: after the last release, a browser could keep the previous stylesheet for a few minutes and show it with the new page. The old stylesheet had no rule for the logo, and I infer that is why it showed huge; I did not reproduce it. The service worker now revalidates the site's own files on every load.

How:
- The public-website pack is adopted. It owns the version scheme and the page stamp, and the github-pages release already bumps the version when this pack is declared.
- `package.json` is the version record. The footer's `title="version …"` is the stamp the release writes, and `app.js` shows it as text.
- `style.css` gives the body a fixed grid (52px / 1fr / 1cm) with overflow hidden; the columns scroll.
- `sw.js` answers the site's own requests with `fetch(…, {cache: "no-cache"})`.
- The logo SVG carries explicit width and height, so no browser falls back to a default size.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` mentions the version.

Checks:
- In Chromium at 1600×900, 1280×720 and 1000×650 with a slide found:
  - the page height equals the window's;
  - the header is 52 px, the footer 38 px (1 cm) and the logo 36 px;
  - both side bars and the image scroll on their own.
- The page's own style.css and app.js now come through the service worker.
- The world check passes with 0 blocking findings.

toolu_01Umyx9qvK3iLhYwKhfj38GG.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- In Ariel's browser the logo showed huge, the status bar was tall, and the whole page scrolled.
- Windows narrower than 1100 px stacked the columns.
- The site version was not shown anywhere.

After:
- The frame is fixed. The 52 px header, the three columns and a 1 cm footer fill the window exactly, and only the left bar, the main box and the right bar scroll. Narrower windows get narrower side bars instead of stacked columns.
- The logo is 36 px high inside the header.
- The footer ends with the site version, e.g. "v1.0.0". It shows 1.0.0 until the first release after this merges.

Stale files: after the last release, a browser could keep the previous stylesheet for a few minutes and show it with the new page. The old stylesheet had no rule for the logo, and I infer that is why it showed huge; I did not reproduce it. The service worker now revalidates the site's own files on every load.

How:
- The public-website pack is adopted. It owns the version scheme and the page stamp, and the github-pages release already bumps the version when this pack is declared.
- `package.json` is the version record. The footer's `title="version …"` is the stamp the release writes, and `app.js` shows it as text.
- `style.css` gives the body a fixed grid (52px / 1fr / 1cm) with overflow hidden; the columns scroll.
- `sw.js` answers the site's own requests with `fetch(…, {cache: "no-cache"})`.
- The logo SVG carries explicit width and height, so no browser falls back to a default size.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` mentions the version.

Checks:
- In Chromium at 1600×900, 1280×720 and 1000×650 with a slide found:
  - the page height equals the window's;
  - the header is 52 px, the footer 38 px (1 cm) and the logo 36 px;
  - both side bars and the image scroll on their own.
- The page's own style.css and app.js now come through the service worker.
- The world check passes with 0 blocking findings.

Your follow-ups are on a new PR, #230, which needs your go-ahead to merge and release once its checks pass. I checked it at 1600×900, 1280×720 and 1000×650:

# HTML - **Injected block markup inside a `

` silently empties it — read the sibling, not the tag.** A block element (a `

`, etc.) inside a `

` is disallowed by the HTML content model, so wherever the two are parsed **together** — document parsing, `DOMParser`, or `innerHTML` on an *ancestor* — the parser (browser or jsdom, same rule) auto-closes the `

` right before the block, which lands as the `

`'s **next sibling** and leaves the tag empty when nothing else was in it. Read `element.nextElementSibling`. Writing *into* an already-parsed `

` (`p.innerHTML`, `p.insertAdjacentHTML`) is the exception — it is the fragment's context element, never in button scope, so the block stays nested instead. - **An ambiguous numeric slash date can't be resolved from its digits — infer the document's convention once, don't guess per-field.** When both parts are ≤ 12 (e.g. `05/07/2026`), resolve the order once per document — never per source or per field — in this order. (1) **An unambiguous sibling date fixes the page's convention**: a slash date elsewhere on the same page with a part > 12 (e.g. `24/07/2026`) parses only one way, and a page is almost always internally consistent — read that date's order and apply it to every other slash date on the page. (2) Failing that, **read the declared locale** (``, `og:locale`): default **month-first** (the order `Date` and most JS parsers assume) and flip to day-first only on a *positive* non-US signal — a non-US region in `lang` / `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` with unknown region stays month-first. The `.` / `-` separators are day-first regardless. - **When code must react to how a real page actually behaves, investigate it live before you ship — don't deploy a hypothesis you can only test after release.** If a change hinges on the real DOM, computed styles, or runtime state of a page you can't see, hand the user one JavaScript snippet to run in the browser DevTools console and read its output back. Reserve "test it after it's deployed" for behavior you've verified genuinely can't be observed now. - **Make that console request a snippet, not an essay.** Send exactly one code block to paste into the console and ask the user to paste its output back. Skip the prose explaining what you're hoping to learn.

# Public website

- **Writing a version number into a page** — don't: `title="version …"` is generated from
  `package.json` by the pack's bump, and a hand-typed stamp names a build that was never served.
  Repair a drifted one, consuming no version number, with

  ```
  node .claudinite/shared/packs/public-website/bump-version.mjs --stamp-only
  ```

- **Deciding how long a published asset may be cached** — publish a manifest naming every asset
  and a hash of its contents, fetch that on each load and evict the entries whose hash moved,
  rather than giving each file a TTL guessed from how fast you think it changes.

- **Caching a freshness manifest, or judging an asset stale by its size** — neither works: nothing
  can attest to its own freshness, so the expected hash must come from a file fetched fresher than
  the one it judges, and a uniform correction is routinely byte-length-neutral.

- **Splitting a payload so each half caches on its own schedule** — have each half record the
  other's generation and refetch both on a mismatch, because every visitor eventually holds one
  half from Tuesday and the other from Thursday; then assert on the join *rate*, since a partial
  join is silent.

- **Judging a failed fetch survivable because the value "just shows as unknown"** — trace it to
  what it draws first. An absent value reaching a boolean, a comparison or a status lookup is
  usually indistinguishable from a real negative, so the page renders a confident falsehood with
  nothing logged. Where it isn't survivable, fail the load and show the error state.

input.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- A line under the image explained what a click does.
- The main toolbar showed four loose checkboxes and plain zoom buttons.
- The views were switched by "View individual items" / "View image".
- The theme button had a text label.
- The footer ran as one flat line.
- Padding and corner rounding varied from place to place, and the image sat edge to edge between the column borders.
- "Restore filter defaults" was a full button.
- The layers were called red, green and blue.
- The site version was 1.10928.1.

After:
- The hint is gone. The mouse becomes a pointer over any candidate.
- The overlay options sit in a "Show ▾" dropdown, which closes when you click elsewhere.
- Zoom is one segmented control: − 2× +.
- The switch reads "Item View" and "Image View".
- The theme button is an icon only: a sun in dark mode and a moon in light mode.
- The footer has sections with dividers: the file name in bold, then bold counts, then timings. Progress sits on the right, and the version is a small tag.
- Spacing and corners follow one scale:
  - one 12 px gutter around and between the three columns;
  - 12 px corners on panels (the image is now a panel too), 8 px on controls and cards, 6 px on chips;
  - roomier inputs and buttons.
- "restore defaults" is a link.
- The layers are named by what they image: Nav1.6, Caspr and DAPI. Each has a tooltip saying what it marks.
- The version is 0.10928.1, and the next release makes it 0.10928.2.

How:
- The spacing and radii are CSS variables (`--pad`, `--r-panel`, `--r-ctl`, `--r-chip`).
- The release carries the major number over from `package.json`, so setting it to 0 there (and re-stamping with `bump-version.mjs --stamp-only`) moves every later release to 0.x.

Checks:
- In Chromium (dark and light), with the reference slide found:
  - unticking "measuring lines" in the menu still hides them;
  - the menu closes on an outside click;
  - the cursor is a pointer over a candidate;
  - the switch label flips both ways.
- The world check passes, including the version-stamp check.

---
name: red-first-finder
description: nor_rf.py red-first NoR finder (v9): rectangular red bricks, several green pairs per red, post-hoc blue mask; scores vs traffic-light
metadata:
  type: project
---

2026-09-27, Ariel asked for three changes, all built in /mnt/project-files/nor-detection/nor_rf.py:
1. The blue mask is applied post hoc. The finder sees the whole image, and a pass fails 'in nucleus' (N) when at least 80% of its red lies on the mask. The rule is red-only because some labelled NoRs have a paranode brushing a nucleus.
2. Several candidates per red blob. Every pair of touching greens at least 110° apart becomes a candidate. The best passing candidate claims its pixels first (quality = snr x sqrt(bright balance x area balance)). There is one NoR per red and one per pixel.
3. Red-first. Red peaks and watershed basins are found on red only. Each red grows from 0.9 down to 0.4 of its peak while it stays brick-like: moment fill >= 0.85 and perimeter ratio <= 1.1 (rectangle 1.0, triangle 0.85/1.1+). Blobs under 1 unit² are not judged. A red that fails at every size is K 'red not rectangular'.

Scores (lab labels): rf P 0.86 R 0.60 with 207 passes; tl P 0.87 R 0.65 with 229 passes. tl_post (tl with the post-hoc blue mask) matches tl, with 247 passes. rf's main loss is A (one green): the second paranode is fainter than the green level. Lowering g_low made results worse (dim rejects). Outputs are in Slide5_Slice1_up_left2/v9_red_first/ (overlay_yellow, review_sheets, diff_vs_tl). Run with `python3 nor_rf.py`. Needs the repo's src on the path: clone to /home/user/missingbulb/norfinder. See [[nor-lab-tool]], [[perf-pass-preference]].

Update 2026-09-27 evening. After Ariel's request for data-based keep/drop decisions (nor_lab.py ablate), the rectangle rule and patch split were dropped (switches kept) and the far-paranode rescue was added (far_u=2). rf is now 48 tp / 9 fp vs tl 47/7: a tie (P(better) 0.48), so tl stays the default. Full verdict table: nor-detection/lab/ledger.md. Outputs: v10_red_first_rescue/.

---
name: three-segment-validation
description: Ariel's NoR validation rules (3 segments G-R-G, greens separate, <10% other colour) and nor3.py status on Slide5
metadata:
  type: project
  modified: 2026-09-25T20:21:43.467Z
---

Ariel (2026-09-25) asked for each NoR to be outlined as 3 segments (green-red-green) and validated. A valid NoR has one red and two greens, in green-red-green order, with the two greens not touching. Each segment must be about 90% pure: under 10% of a segment's pixels may be the other colour, or an intensity-ratio equivalent. Ariel said to use this validation as the score for judging the segmentation.

This is implemented in /mnt/project-files/nor-detection/nor3.py, which reuses naive_nor.py's load and blue_mask. Settings: pixel classes by dominance, green_frac 0.09, red_frac 0.04, no smoothing. """Traffic-light candidate finder.

Told to a child: cut a little stamp out of card with three windows in a row, green, red,
green, like a traffic light lying on its side. Slide the stamp over the whole picture, turn it
every way, and pull the green windows a bit closer or further apart. Wherever each window
shows its own colour (green in the green windows, red in the red one), put a pin. The pins
where the fit is best are the nodes. Then colour in the three blobs under the windows.

The old finder started from a red dot and went looking for greens afterwards, so it often came
back with one green (reason A). Here a spot only becomes a candidate if both greens are already
under the stamp, so a one-green candidate can only happen if colouring in a green fails.
All sizes are in units (median half-length of a green blob)."""
import math, numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
import nor3
from nor3 import classify, finish, resolve_overlaps, EIGHT

411:def segment_fill(caspr, nav, bm, p=P3):
412-    """How to find a node, told to a child:
413-      1. Find a bright red dot.
414-      2. Turn around until you are looking along the fibre: that is the way with green on
415-         BOTH sides of the dot.
416-      3. Walk out each way (a gentle bend is fine). You leave the red and step onto green.
417-         Keep walking while the green gets brighter; you stop once it has faded to half of
418-         the brightest green you saw. The brightest spot is where you "landed".
419-      4. Colour in each of the three blobs like a colouring book, starting from the red dot
420-         and from each landing spot: colour a neighbouring pixel if it is still mostly that
421-         colour and at least half as bright as where you started. Where it gets dimmer than
422-         half, that is the blob's edge.
423-    Stops are relative (half of each blob's own peak), and every distance is in units."""
424-    cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr = classify(caspr, nav, bm, p)
425-    valid_ = ~bm
284:def segment_walk(caspr, nav, bm, p=P2):
285-    """Find a red dot, find which way its fibre runs (the direction with green on BOTH sides),
286-    then walk out both ways along that line: red first, then green on each side.
287-
288-    One candidate per red peak; the axis comes from the greens, so a paranode broken into
289-    speckles by pixel noise is still found as one green segment along the line."""
290-    cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr = classify(caspr, nav, bm, p)
291-    valid_ = ~bm
292-    F = (cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr, valid_)
57:def segment(caspr, nav, bm, p=P):
58-    cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr = classify(caspr, nav, bm, p)
59-    valid_ = ~bm
60-    F = (cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr, valid_)
61-    glab, _ = ndi.label(green, EIGHT)
62-    rlab, nr = ndi.label(red, EIGHT)
63-    gsz = np.bincount(glab.ravel())
64-    # unit: median half-length of green blobs, as in nor.detect
65-    gobj = ndi.find_objects(glab)
99:def segment_rf(caspr, nav, bm, p=PR):
100-    none = bm if p['blue'] == 'pre' else np.zeros_like(bm)   # the finder sees the whole image; blue comes last
101-    cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr = classify(caspr, nav, none, p)
102-    valid_ = ~none; F = (cn, rn, green, red, tg, tr, valid_)
103-    glab, _ = ndi.label(green, EIGHT); gsz = np.bincount(glab.ravel())
104-    lens = [max(sl[0].stop - sl[0].start, sl[1].stop - sl[1].start) / 2
105-            for i, sl in enumerate(ndi.find_objects(glab)) if sl is not None and gsz[i + 1] >= p['min_green']]
106-    unit = float(np.median(lens)); H, W = cn.shape

}

    'strip_u': "Half-width (units) of the strip walked along the fibre.",
    'touch_u': "A green counts as touching the red if it comes this close (units).",

one line per parameter (HELP). tests/test_interactive.py fails when a finder or a parameter the
page shows has no entry here, so a new setting arrives with its explanation.

"unit" is the image's own scale: the median half-length of a green blob, so sizes follow the image
rather than its pixel count."""

    'tl': "Slides a green-red-green stencil over the whole image at every angle and a few spacings, "
          "and marks the spots where all three windows show their own colour. Only spots with both "
          "greens already in place become candidates; then the red and the two greens under the "
          "stencil are coloured in.",
    'rf': "Starts from the red alone: finds every red spot and grows it outwards while it stays "
          "compact. Every green blob touching the red is a possible paranode, and any two on opposite "
          "sides make a candidate, so one red can give several. The best candidate that passes the "
          "filters wins, and no pixel belongs to two NoRs.",
    'fill': "Starts at each bright red dot, turns to face along the fibre (the way with green on both "
            "sides), and walks out each way until it lands on the brightest green. Then colours in the "
            "red and both greens from their peaks, stopping where each drops below a fraction of its "
            "own peak.",
    'walk': "Starts at each red peak, picks the direction with green on both sides, then walks along "
            "that line in a narrow strip: through the red first, then onto the green on each side.",
    'blobs': "The simplest finder: every red blob is paired with the green blobs that touch it. Fast, "
             "but it misses greens that do not quite touch the red.",
}

    # telling colours apart (every finder)
    'green_frac': "Share of the image's pixels that may count as green (the brightest ones). Raise it to pick up fainter paranodes.",
    'red_frac': "Share of the image's pixels that may count as red (the brightest ones). Raise it to pick up fainter nodes.",

input.title: Page: tidier toolbar, footer and spacing; help for every finder and setting; version 0.10928.x
input.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jh?thread=cmsg_01NLfVm5WfzHBRRyA4oMF5jhKUmZ1vDWkaHNc4R6fwWVq9)_

Before:
- A line under the image explained what a click does, and a note said finding takes 10–30 seconds.
- The main toolbar showed four loose checkboxes and plain zoom buttons.
- The views were switched by "View individual items" / "View image".
- The theme button had a text label.
- The footer ran as one flat line.
- Padding and corner rounding varied from place to place.
- "Restore filter defaults" was a full button.
- The layers were called red, green and blue.
- Nothing said how a finder works or what a setting does.
- The site version was 1.10928.1.

After:
- Both notes are gone. The mouse becomes a pointer over any candidate.
- The overlay options sit in a "Show ▾" dropdown, and zoom is one segmented control (− 2× +).
- The switch reads "Item View" and "Image View".
- The theme button is an icon only: a sun in dark mode and a moon in light mode.
- The footer has sections: the file name, bold counts, timings, then progress and a version tag on the right.
- Spacing and corners follow one scale:
  - one 12 px gutter around and between the columns;
  - 12 px corners on panels (the image is now a panel too), 8 px on controls and cards, 6 px on chips.
- "restore defaults" is a link.
- The layers are named Nav1.6, Caspr and DAPI, each with a tooltip saying what it marks.
- Under the finder picker, a few sentences explain how the chosen finder works.
- Every setting and every filter value has a small ?. Hovering or focusing it says what the setting does.
- The version is 0.10928.1, and the next release makes it 0.10928.2.

How:
- The explanations live in `detection/finder_help.py`: `ABOUT` per finder and `HELP` per parameter, written from the code that reads each one. `interactive.describe()` passes them to the page.
- A new test in `tests/test_interactive.py` fails when a finder or any setting the page shows has no explanation, so a new setting must come with one. I watched it fail on a removed entry.
- Spacing and radii are CSS variables (`--pad`, `--r-panel`, `--r-ctl`, `--r-chip`).
- The release carries the major number over from `package.json`, so setting it to 0 there (re-stamped with `bump-version.mjs --stamp-only`) moves later releases to 0.x.
- R8 in `docs/requirements.md` gains the help requirement.

Checks:
- `tests/test_interactive.py` passes; the reference slide still gives 247 passes.
- In Chromium, dark and light:
  - 50 settings each show a ?, and hovering one shows its line;
  - the finder note changes with the finder;
  - the Show menu still hides the lines and closes on an outside click;
  - the cursor is a pointer over a candidate;
  - the view switch flips both ways.
- The world check passes, including the version-stamp check.
